---
title: "When something goes wrong"
description: >-
  Where zotLook writes down why a preview failed, what to check first, and what to put in a bug report.
---

Most of what zotLook does happens in someone else's program — the system's
preview panel — so when nothing appears, the reason is usually one of a few
ordinary things. This page is the order worth checking them in, and where to
find the one file that says what actually happened.

## Nothing happens on Space

**Is the preview program there?** On Linux the plugin drives GNOME Sushi
(`apt install gnome-sushi`); on Windows, [QuickLook](https://github.com/QL-Win/QuickLook),
which has to be **running**. macOS needs nothing installed. The
[Platforms](platforms.qmd) page says what each one can show.

**Is the shortcut still yours?** A combination the system or another
application has claimed never reaches Zotero at all. The recording in
**Settings → zotLook** says so when it happens: press the button, press your
combination, and if nothing arrived it tells you rather than waiting silently.

**Is another plugin on the same key?** zotLook installs beside Guillaume
Chapron's Zotero7QuickLook rather than over it — different plugin IDs — so with
both installed, Space is claimed twice. Pick one.

## The contact sheet fails or comes out empty

zotLook writes down why. Zotero's debug output is shared with every plugin and
a chatty one drowns everything else out, so the last thing the plugin logged
before a failure goes into a file of its own:

::: {.panel-tabset}
### macOS

``` bash
cat "$(getconf DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR)org.zotero.zotero/zotLook/last-failure.log"
```

### Linux

``` bash
cat /tmp/zotero/zotLook/last-failure.log
```

### Windows

``` powershell
type "$env:TEMP\zotero\zotLook\last-failure.log"
```
:::

It holds the plugin's own last two hundred log lines and nothing else — no
document contents, no library data. It is worth attaching to a bug report
verbatim.

The exact temp directory is Zotero's own, so if the paths above do not exist,
**Help → Debug Output Logging → View Output** names it at the top.

## A kept preview looks out of date

It should not: an entry is remade as soon as the file, its annotations or the
settings behind it change. If one is stale anyway, **Settings → zotLook →
Delete kept previews** clears them all, and the next call makes them afresh.
The figure beside the button says what they occupy; after the deletion it reads
zero.

The folder is `zotLook-cache` in the Zotero profile inside the system's cache
directory, and you may delete it by hand with Zotero closed — see
[Settings](settings.qmd).

## The page overview of a book says it has no printed page numbers

That is the honest answer rather than a failure. An EPUB reflows and has no
pages of its own; the numbers a page overview shows belong to a printed edition
and are only there when the publisher carried them into the file — marked in the
text as `epub:type="pagebreak"`, or listed in the navigation. Roughly one book
in eight carries them, and those are mostly the academic ones: Springer,
O'Reilly, textbooks.

Where they are missing, nothing can supply them, and a sheet cut at arbitrary
points would be worse than none. Use the ordinary preview (**Space**) to read
the book.

## An EPUB annotation is listed but not marked in the text

The annotation list behind the button in the corner shows every annotation; one that could not be placed in
the page is shown as such rather than left out. That happens when the position
Zotero stored no longer resolves — most often because the book itself has
changed since the annotation was made, so the chapter or the element it names
is no longer where it was.

## Reporting it

Please open an issue: **<https://github.com/fre-ms/zotLook/issues/new?template=bug_report.yml>**

What helps most:

- your operating system and version, and your Zotero version;
- what you pressed and what you expected;
- `last-failure.log` if the contact sheet or an EPUB was involved;
- for an EPUB, whether the book is one you can share — the awkward ones are
  usually awkward in a way no description conveys.

zotLook is tested on macOS, Windows and Linux, but on a narrow set of versions.
Other combinations will turn up things. I cannot promise to fix everything, but
a report with the file above in it is usually enough to see what happened.

An idea for what zotLook should do is welcome too — see
[Feature requests](requests.qmd).
